english.title: Possess offensive weapon on school / further education premises
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without good reason or lawful authority, had with you on

(A)_[school]_
(B)_[further education]_

premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), an offensive weapon within the meaning of section 1 of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953, namely **(..SPECIFY WEAPON..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139A(2) and (5) of the Criminal Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
had with them
on school premises / further education premises
an offensive weapon within the meaning of Section 1 of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) 'offensive weapon' is defined in section 1 of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 as any article made or adapted for use for causing injury to the person, or intended by the person having it with him for such use by him, or by some other person.
(ii) 'school premises' is defined in section 139A(6) as land used for the purposes of a school excluding any land occupied solely as a dwelling by a person employed at the school.
(iii) 'further education premises' is defined in 139A(6A) as land used solely for the purposes of an institution within the further education section or a 16-19 academy.
(iv) For possession of offensive weapon in a public place see offence wording H486 and offence wording H20299 for possession in private.
(v) A defence is available at section 1(4) if a person can prove he had the weapon for the use at work, educational purposes, religious reason or as part of any national costume.
(vi) Section 139A was amended to extend the offence to cover not only school premises but also further education premises; for offences committed before 6th April 2022 please see H4431.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 139A(5)(a) and (5ZA) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
Sections 139A(5A) -(5E) outline provisions requiring a court to impose an appropriate custodial sentence in certain cases.
